topic: A person learns their favorite restaurant is closing
text:
You step into the office, rain dripping off your hat, and there's a heaviness to the air, like the city’s got an extra layer of fog tonight. You drop into the chair across from me, your coat still humming with the chill of the street. “They’re closing down the Blue Plate, Sammy. It’s done,” you say, like you’ve just lost an old friend.

I lean back, let the silence stretch a bit. “Reckon nothing lasts forever, but places like that, they’re more than just walls and plates. They’re a piece of you, a piece of this city. Hard to let go.”

You nod, slow and thoughtful, maybe remembering the first time you walked in, the smell of fried onions cutting through the air, or the way the light used to hit the jukebox in the corner. “Yeah, Sammy. Maybe we’ll open up our own place one day. Better than the Blue Plate, even.”

I smile, a rare thing these days. “You got a deal, pal. Just as soon as we figure out where the last of the crooks are hiding their loot.”
